plan.summary: Design-only review of three matched workflow-policy approaches and four modification tasks. No registered checks: checks=[]; no runtime or model experiment.

findings.evidence: Source grounding is coordinator-reported; shared policy grammar and mappings are future prerequisites.
findings.recommendation: Review design only; do not approve unimplemented execution or claim maintenance benefit.

tasks.deliverable: Independent design feasibility and methods assessment
tasks.verification: Preserve blockers; mark omitted source unverified.

tasks.deliverable: Frozen design, review record and continuation state
tasks.verification: Separate proposed changes from actual work; no paid calls or live workflow modification.

methods.summary: Ready for the bounded design handoff only. The proposed strong JSON baselines, separation of externalization from representation, preserved failures and limited maintenance claims are appropriate. Execution readiness and repository grounding remain unverified; no checks were run.

findings.evidence: The grounding observation about RUNBOOK and research_ops.evidence_for is explicitly coordinator-reported without source excerpts.
findings.recommendation: Treat this observation as unverified until the next contract includes a minimal traceable source-field mapping and relevant source excerpts; do not describe this design review as validation of live workflow behavior.

findings.evidence: The procedure defers the abstract rule language, unknown precedence and temporal/dependency semantics. The shared_evidence_update task requires both exact transitive invalidation and unknown when dependency coverage is missing.
findings.recommendation: Before implementation freeze dependency edge direction, version identity, coverage scope, cycles, duplicate/out-of-order event semantics and how unknown combines with a known blocking condition. Include an incomplete-coverage example where unrelatedness cannot be established, so absent edges do not silently mean unaffected.

findings.evidence: B versus C is a representation/tooling comparison and the primary measures include hidden host-code bypass; engineering measures split evaluator, adapter, model and policy changes.
findings.recommendation: Specify evaluator/adapter boundaries and a common supported operation inventory before coding. Record each arm's unsupported operation and any bespoke extension, including initial costs, rather than comparing only successful matched cases or attributing custom evaluator advantages to serialization.

findings.evidence: The procedure preserves first attempts and repairs, counterbalances arm order, and labels authored tests as software expectations. Measures explicitly reject human-productivity claims from time or line counts.
findings.recommendation: Keep task-by-arm denominators, unknown outcomes, first-attempt correctness and repaired correctness separately visible. Operationalize acceptable setup burden before interpreting the continuation gate; otherwise present it as a qualitative engineering decision.

tasks.deliverable: Next-step shared contract defining dependency coverage, version/event semantics, unknown precedence, supported operations and component boundaries, with one traceable real source-field mapping.
tasks.verification: Independently review the contract and representative counterexamples before implementing or executing any arm; retain the current design-only status and unverified grounding until evidence is supplied.

implementation.summary: Ready as a design-only handoff to specification of the shared contract. The proposed arms and immutable historical decisions are implementable in principle, but no execution, source mapping, checks or resource suitability has been verified.

findings.evidence: RUNBOOK behavior and evidence_for gates are coordinator-reported without source excerpts. No ledger schema, source hash or concrete field mapping is supplied.
findings.recommendation: Before implementation, freeze a sanitized shadow export with provenance and hashes, document one verified source-field mapping and distinguish declared complete dependency coverage from merely observed links. Do not infer live workflow compatibility from this review.

findings.evidence: The design explicitly defers the shared grammar, unknown precedence, version binding and dependency semantics. These determine whether the three arms implement equivalent behavior.
findings.recommendation: The next contract must specify typed identity and versions, relation direction, cycle termination, duplicate and out-of-order event handling, missing-policy behavior, exception precedence and the separation of immutable historical results from current eligibility. Define SHACL failure versus unsupported or incomplete evaluation consistently with JSON.

findings.evidence: A has indexed JSON and shared policies; B and C receive the same rules and relations. Setup costs and evaluator, adapter, model, policy and test edits are recorded separately.
findings.recommendation: Retain these boundaries and freeze the explanation/output contract before implementation. Record unsupported operations and host-code special cases rather than quietly adding capabilities to only one arm. B-C remains a representation/tooling comparison, not a pure serialization effect.

findings.evidence: No trial size, export bound, implementation retry limit or concrete timing/logging schema is supplied. The 16GiB host resource assumptions are unverified, and checks=[] means no checks have run.
findings.recommendation: Before an execution review, set bounded input sizes, retry/repair accounting, artifact manifests and a consistent editing/verification timing method. Preserve first attempts and all repairs. No tests are needed for this design-only artifact; later implementations require matched invariant and negative-control checks.

findings.evidence: The scope excludes actual approvals, live gate changes, databases, paid calls and publication; host race handling is explicitly unexercised.
findings.recommendation: Keep the next step read-only and offline. Treat engineering effort traces as descriptive and obtain a separate implementation/execution review before claiming measured workflow benefits.
